📍 Workplace: All work takes place at our company headquarters in Kastrup.

Shape the future of education technology

At IST, we're building the cloud platform that powers educational solutions used by more than five million users across Europe. Unlike most cloud teams, we run our own cloud — on our own hardware, in our own data center. That means the abstraction stops with us: when a node misbehaves, there's no support ticket to a hyperscaler.

There's a rack, and someone who knows it.

We're looking for a Cloud Engineer who finds that appealing rather than daunting.

About the role

As a Cloud Engineer, you'll help design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform — from the automation and orchestration layers our developers build on, all the way down to the switches, servers and cabling that carry it. You'll do this together with our Cloud Engineering team, architects, developers and stakeholders, whether the work happens at a keyboard or in a rack.

In practice, around a quarter of your time will be spent physically on site in the data center. Not as a separate duty, but as a natural part of the work: expanding capacity for a new cluster the team has just automated, replacing a switch that's been throwing errors in your own monitoring, tracing a network issue that turns out to be a cable rather than a config. Owning the platform end to end is what makes this role different from a pure cloud position.

The role is based at our office in Roskilde, Denmark, with the primary data center within reach. Some travel is required, primarily to our office in Växjö, Sweden.

Key responsibilities

• Design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform across the full stack — from physical hardware to the self-service tooling our developers use

• Automate VMs, containers, storage and networking using Ansible, Terraform, Puppet and PowerShell DSC

• Plan and carry out capacity expansions: from sizing and procurement to racking, cabling, provisioning and putting the capacity into production

• Diagnose and resolve issues wherever they originate — including replacing switches, disks and other failed components on site, and handling firmware, BIOS and driver lifecycle across the fleet

• Support reliable, scalable developer platforms, CI/CD pipelines, orchestration and self-service tools

• Manage databases, object storage and monitoring/logging stacks, with observability that spans both the platform and the hardware underneath it

• Contribute to access, identity and compliance work in line with ISO, PCI and internal policies, including physical access and site security

• Ensure robust backup and disaster recovery plans are in place, tested against real hardware failure scenarios

• Coordinate with hardware vendors and support partners (Dell, Cisco and similar) on spare parts, RMAs and escalations

Your profile

You have a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, network engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, along with solid experience in cloud engineering, infrastructure automation and DevOps practices.

Just as importantly, you're comfortable at both ends of the stack. You can discuss platform architecture with our developers in the morning and spend the afternoon in the rack with a screwdriver, and you see those as the same job rather than two different ones. Working in a data center environment — noisy, cold, occasionally at short notice — is something you take in stride.

We also look for:

• Hands-on experience with server, storage and network hardware — Cisco, Dell, KVM, VMware or similar

• Practical understanding of data center fundamentals: power, cooling, rack design, structured cabling

• Strong knowledge of security, compliance and governance in cloud environments

• Strategic thinking and the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

• A collaborative, decisive and pragmatic approach to problem-solving

• A valid driver's license and the ability to reach the data center when needed

What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. We apply an office-first policy, and given the hands-on nature of this role, regular physical presence at the office and in the datacenter is part of the job. Within that framework, there's room for flexibility on the days where your work doesn't require you on site.

You'll join an international and collaborative environment where you'll have real ownership, influence over strategic technology decisions, and the chance to help shape the future of learning.

Apply

Applications are reviewed continuously. For questions, contact Bengt Welin bengt.welin@ist.com or HR@ist.com. Please note that a background check is part of the recruitment process.

Welcome to apply!

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time.

The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data.

The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project.

Responsibilities

• Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data.
• Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction.
• Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits.
• Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities.
• Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging.
• Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects.
• Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Qualifications
You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English.

To succeed in this position, you are expected to have:

• A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline.
• A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models.
• Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks.
• A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage:

• Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations.
• Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion.
• Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning.
• Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling.
• Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction.
• Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. 
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute
DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Entrepreneurship, AI, and Labor Market Disruption - DTU Entrepreneurship
jobs.description:
Are you interested in exploring the following questions? 

• How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship?
• How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance?
• How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts?
DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption.

The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece.

The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope.

Your tasks will include:

• Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions.
• Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes.
• Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data.
• Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners.
• Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals.
• Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders.
• Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners.
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change.

We expect you to have:

• A Master’s degree.
• A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills.
• Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
• The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment.
The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required:

• Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data.
• Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

jobs.occupation: Data Migration Consultant to Scan Global Logistics
jobs.description:
Join an International Transformation Program at Scan Global Logistics

Are you detail-oriented, analytical, and passionate about working with data? Do you enjoy identifying errors, improving data quality, and ensuring that information is accurate and ready for use?

jobs.occupation: 2-Year Postdoctoral Position in Modeling of Microbial Soil Carbon Cycling
jobs.description:
Postdoc of genome-informed microbial biogeochemical modeling

  Department of Biology

  Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  Soils store 2300 Pg of organic carbon – three times as much as in the atmosphere. Yet, the fate of these huge carbon stocks under global warming remains highly uncertain. Although microorganisms are key players in soil carbon decomposition, large-scale models ignore microbial processes due to difficulty of quantifying microbial traits that can inform models. To overcome this limitation, the aim of this position is to quantify microbial traits from metagenomes to develop a microbial-explicit version of the dynamic vegetation model LPJ-GUESS.

  You will join a dynamic team at the Center of Excellence VOLT (Center for Volatile interactions, https://volt.ku.dk/) consisting of microbial ecologists, biogeochemists and ecosystem modelers. We offer a creative and stimulating working environment in a collaborative, international research group. We have state-of-the art laboratory facilities and bioninformatics pipelines for analyses of microbial communities and biogeochemical fluxes. Our team also comprises specialists in process-based ecosystem modeling with whom you will closely collaborate. We provide access to supercomputing facilities to carry out bioinformatics and modeling tasks.

  You will work with microbial genomes and metagenomes to predict microbial traits relevant for carbon cycling and modeling using computational structural biology tools to infer protein function. These tasks will use public databases as well as environmental metagenomic datasets produced by the group. You will moreover work with the process-based ecosystem model LPJ-GUESS to implement microbial decomposition of soil organic matter.

  We seek an ambitious and highly motivated candidate with a PhD in computational biology, environmental sciences or related fields. A successful candidate should have a strong background in environmental microbial ecology and bioinformatics as well as experience in advanced statistical analyses and programming with R, python or similar. Moreover, experience with process-based modeling is a plus. Fluency in written and spoken English is a requirement, as well as excellent writing skills demonstrated by the publication record. The candidate should be comfortable working in teams with a collaborative mindset.

  Further information on the Department of Biology is linked at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/ and on the recruiting unit at https://volt.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Jonathan Donhauser, jonathan.donhauser@bio.ku.dk

  The position is open from 1/2/2027 or as soon as possible thereafter and is for 2 years.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

   

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

   

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter describing the motivation for the position 	
• Curriculum vitae (maximum 2 pages) 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of research plan (max. 3 pages) 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact details (name, address, telephone & email) of 2 professional referees   
 The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

   

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Medical & Translational Science

As Medical Project Director, you will help shape our cardiovascular therapy area strategy and provide medical and scientific input to business development opportunities. You will combine detailed assessment of individual assets with a portfolio perspective on what we need to develop over the next five and ten years. Working with colleagues across the value chain, you will identify opportunities, assess risks and uncertainties, and turn scientific and strategic insights into clear recommendations for leadership and portfolio decisions.

What you’ll bring

You bring strong medical and scientific expertise and sound strategic judgement. You can zoom in to understand the details and uncertainties in a dataset and zoom out to assess what they mean for an opportunity and the wider portfolio. You distinguish what the evidence supports from what remains uncertain, challenge assumptions constructively and make balanced recommendations when information is incomplete.

• A Medical Doctor degree and strong research experience at PhD level or equivalent are mandatory.

• A minimum of five years of clinical development experience is expected, together with the ability to critically assess preclinical and clinical evidence. Experience with cardiovascular disease is an advantage.

• A strong understanding of the pharmaceutical value chain, including how research, clinical development, regulatory requirements, CMC and commercial considerations influence development and portfolio decisions.

• Experience in business development or therapy area strategy is preferred. Hands-on business development experience assessing individual assets, for example through screening or due diligence, is particularly valuable.

• Experience guiding work across functions, engaging senior leaders and building agreement around priorities without relying on formal authority.

• Strong communication, presentation and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain complex scientific issues clearly in written and spoken English to colleagues with different professional backgrounds.

• Experience engaging external medical and scientific experts to inform development strategies and interpretation of evidence would be useful.

What you’ll do

• Help shape cardiovascular therapy area strategy and portfolio priorities over the next five and ten years, identifying gaps and opportunities for internal development and external innovation.

• Provide medical and scientific input to screening and due diligence of potential business development opportunities, assessing biological rationale, evidence for clinical benefit, potential differentiation, and key risks and uncertainties.

Who you’ll work with

You will work closely with cardiovascular leadership, Global Project Teams and colleagues in Research, Clinical Development, Business Development, Commercial, Regulatory Affairs and CMC. Across these relationships, you will listen openly, bring different perspectives together and build the agreement needed to move strategies and plans forward.

You can expect a high degree of independence, complex scientific and strategic questions, and the opportunity to influence decisions with substantial portfolio and business impact. You will take initiative, follow through on agreed actions and contribute to a collaborative environment where colleagues share knowledge and challenge each other constructively.

We will provide relevant training, onboarding and support to help you grow into the role and further develop your skills in therapy area strategy and business development. You will build on your medical and scientific experience while learning from colleagues across the value chain. Priorities may change as new evidence emerges, and you will help the team adapt its recommendations and plans.

A PhD in cell biology, molecular biology, biotechnology, pharmacology or a related discipline.

The Department of Science Education at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position starting 1 March 2027. The postdoc position will be a part of the SPINE project (Strengthening Pathways and Infrastructures for Navigating Interdisciplinary Collaboration in Existing Academic Structures), funded by the Lundbeck Foundation

  We are looking for an engaged and independent researcher to help us develop and test practical ways of strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration in research and education.

  The SPINE project investigates how interdisciplinary collaboration can be better supported within existing academic structures. The project combines qualitative research, international fieldwork, and participatory action research to develop practical “plug-and-play” tools, such as methods, templates, games, and workshop formats, that can be readily used by researchers, educators, and research organisations.

   

  Your role

  As a postdoc in SPINE, you will lead the testing and refinement of tools and methods at SPINE’s test sites, including designing and facilitating intervention workshops with researchers and other stakeholders. You will evaluate and adapt approaches across different contexts and help turn research findings into practical, “plug-and-play” resources for interdisciplinary collaboration.

  The position combines research and reporting on the development and testing activities with qualitative research, but the main emphasis will be on the development, testing, and refinement of practical tools and interventions.

   

  You will also contribute to:

   	
• Conducting qualitative research and fieldwork 	
• Analysing and evaluating empirical material and interventions 	
• Working with project partners and stakeholders 	
• Disseminating findings through academic and practice-oriented outputs 	
• Teaching at the Department of Science Education   The position is based in Denmark, where most work will take place. Some international travel will be required for fieldwork, test-site visits, and collaboration with project partners.

   

  Who we are looking for

  We are looking for a researcher interested in how interdisciplinary collaboration works in practice, with the ability to move between research, facilitation, and development.

   

  You should have:

   	
• The ability to work independently while contributing actively to a collaborative team 	
• Strong written and oral communication skills 	
• Willingness and ability to travel internationally when required    

  We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following:

   	
• Interdisciplinary higher education research 	
• Participatory action research or co-design 	
• Workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement 	
• Developing or evaluating practical approaches to research and collaboration 	
• Translating research into practical or policy-relevant outputs 	
• Spoken or written Danish, which is an advantage but not a requirement   We welcome candidates from different disciplinary and methodological backgrounds and do not expect applicants to meet every criterion.

   

  What we offer

  You will join an international and collaborative research environment in central Copenhagen and become part of a project with a strong focus on research that makes a practical difference.

  The SPINE project is led by Associate Professor Katrine Ellemose Lindvig at the Section for Higher Education Research and Development, Department of Science Education, University of Copenhagen. The SPINE team consists of the PI, one postdoc, and one PhD student, and works closely with colleagues in a wider research group on Interdisciplinary Higher Education, which includes an additional PhD student. As postdoc, you will work closely together with the researchers in SPINE and this wider group, while also collaborating with external partners and stakeholders.

Do you have a strong interest in cyber security and enjoy turning new insights and knowledge into ways of improvement? At Collectia, we are looking for a hands-on security professional with the ability to work across a broad technical remit and help move our security programme forward.

In this role, you will be the main contributor across a range of cyber security initiatives, working closely with experienced colleagues in DevOps, Engineering and IT Support, as well as external specialists. The position covers infrastructure, cloud, identity, endpoints and operational processes, combining technical security engineering with governance and compliance. You will help define effective controls and make sure they are implemented in practice.

Your key responsibilities

• Own and continuously develop our CIS 18 framework, including gap assessments, prioritised action plans, implementation follow-up and maturity reporting.

• Own and improve our Microsoft Secure Score and drive relevant security improvements across Microsoft 365 and Azure.

• Act as a central technical partner for ISAE 3000 activities, including audit preparation, evidence collection, control walkthroughs and remediation.

• Establish, document, maintain and test internal IT and security controls, ensuring that control design and evidence remain practical, consistent and traceable.

• Perform security risk assessments and drive remediation plans through to completion in collaboration with relevant colleagues.

• Plan, coordinate and carry out penetration tests and attack simulations together with external security experts and ethical hackers, and translate findings into concrete improvements with our technical teams.

• Investigate and implement technical security improvements based on developments in threats, vulnerabilities and defensive capabilities.

• Support the handling of security incidents, including investigation, containment, lessons learned and improvements to controls, monitoring and procedures.

Security domains in scope

The role spans identity and privileged access management, multifactor authentication, vulnerability management, logging and detection, incident management, endpoint and network security, server hardening, and cloud security across Microsoft 365 and Azure. It also includes security controls, risk management and audit readiness.

You will be part of

You will join our DevOps department in a role with significant influence on how security is designed, implemented and operated. You will work closely with technical colleagues and relevant business stakeholders, with direct access to decision-makers and opportunity to shape our security roadmap and ways of working.

We offer high professional standards, short decision paths, and opportunities for continuous professional development and knowledge sharing. Benefits include a lunch scheme, pension, health insurance, an in-house hairdresser and masseur, carwash and fitness subscription.

How we imagine you

Above all, you have a strong interest in cyber security. You are curious about emerging threats, new technologies and security developments, and you enjoy investigating how things work, and turning that knowledge into practical improvements.

We are open to different levels of experience. If you are earlier in your cyber security career but have a strong technical foundation, the right mindset and the ambition to grow into broader ownership, we would still be very interested in hearing from you.

You bring:

• Hands-on experience in cyber security, infrastructure security or a comparable technical security role.

• An interest in working across multiple security domains, with the initiative to investigate unfamiliar issues and involve the right colleagues or specialists when needed.

• An understanding of Microsoft security capabilities across Microsoft 365, Entra ID and Azure, including Secure Score, identity protection and privileged access.

• A practical approach to risk, balancing security, operational impact, cost and business priorities.

• The ability to take ownership, manage several initiatives at once and follow actions through to completion.

• Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical specialists and non-technical stakeholders in Danish and English.

Experience with control frameworks such as CIS 18, and with audit preparation or remediation in an ISAE 3000, ISO 27001, NIS2 or similar environment is an advantage.

You do not need to be a specialist in every security domain from day one. What matters most is that you enjoy being hands-on, stay curious, challenge existing configurations constructively and work with others to implement sustainable improvements.
